docs.title: /replyreviewer — Peer reviewer response generator
docs.text:
Generates a formal LaTeX response letter per reviewer comment file and applies track-change markup directly in the paper using the changes package. The reviewer ID (id=RN) in each \added, \replaced, or \deleted command is the permanent, visible link between the paper modification and the response letter. Delegates to the reviewer-response agent.

Full command syntax:

/replyreviewer --paper <paper.tex> --reviewers <r1.txt> [r2.txt ...] [--title "Title"] [--editor "Name"]

Example: 

/replyreviewer --paper sn-article.tex --reviewers .\reviewers\R1.txt .\reviewers\R2.txt --editor "Zhouping Yin"

Argument Required Description --paper <path.tex> Yes Path to the original LaTeX paper --reviewers <files> Yes One .txt file per reviewer; first = R1, second = R2, etc. --title "..." No Paper title for the letter header; extracted from \title{} if omitted --editor "..." No Editor name for the salutation; defaults to [EDITOR NAME] if omitted

What the agent produces:

  1. One LaTeX response letter per reviewer — <basename>_response_R<N>.tex, each with a formal opening, General Comments, point-by-point Specific Comments, and a Scopus-validated References Added section with clickable DOIs.
  2. Annotated original paper — \added[id=RN]{} / \replaced[id=RN]{}{} / \deleted[id=RN]{} markup, grammar-only fixes applied directly, and \usepackage{changes} with one \definechangesauthor per reviewer (R1 blue, R2 red, R3 orange, R4+ purple) added to the preamble automatically.

Comment categories processed:

Code Category Paper change G Grammar / spelling Direct fix, no markup S Style / writing \replaced[id=RN]{new}{old} SC Scientific issue \added[id=RN]{...} M Methodology addition \added[id=RN]{...} R Results addition \added[id=RN]{...} D Discussion addition \added[id=RN]{...} FT Figure / table issue \added[id=RN]{...} new float EQ Equation issue \replaced[id=RN]{}{} or \deleted[id=RN]{} REF Reference suggestion Scopus-validated, \added[id=RN]{\cite{}} Q General quality \added[id=RN]{...} MAJ Major revision \replaced[id=RN]{}{} / \deleted[id=RN]{}

Prerequisites: SCOPUS_API_KEY set; campus network or VPN active.

Related commands: /auditpaper (full audit before/after revision), /bibclean (clean the .bib after adding references), /ref (format individual references).

docs.title: ThesisTracker Integration
docs.text:
Chapter 09 of the ResearchTools manual. Back to table of contents.

This repository is one half of a two-repository system. The other half, JdUmuhoza/ThesisTracker, is where the form catalogue, field maps, and the student-facing UI/UX live (see the 2026 roadmap item in 00-purpose.md). Neither repository's .claude/CLAUDE.md or this manual duplicates that project's own documentation; this chapter is only the map of where the two meet, so the relationship stays discoverable instead of being findable only by reading Architecture.md prose.

docs.title: Two files named alike, two different scopes
docs.text:
• Architecture.md — this repository's own agent/skill/command architecture, seven layers, entirely internal to ResearchTools.
  • NEW_ARCHITECTURE.md — the shared architecture document for the UQAC form engine, the system the two repositories make up together. It is MEANT to be committed identically to main in both repositories (byte-for-byte, checked by sha256sum), so either checkout tells the whole story — except for a known divergence between the two checkouts' copies as of 2026-10-02, which this file's own opening paragraph names; reconciling them is the operator's job. It carries the twenty-two planned units (RT-* on this side, TT-* on ThesisTracker's), their delivery status, and the data model and lifecycle both sides agree on. That content is deliberately not repeated here: a second copy is exactly the kind of drift this manual split exists to avoid (see 00-purpose.md).

docs.title: The boundary: form-service
docs.text:
The dependency between the two systems runs one way only: ThesisTracker calls the form service, never the reverse. ThesisTracker itself does not belong to this repository's own component graph and is a separate system.

deploy/form-service/ (the form-service skill, chapter 04) wraps the PDF ingest, widget-dump, filling, and PAdES-signing scripts in a stateless FastAPI application, so ThesisTracker calls one HTTP service (/pdf/widgets, /pdf/fill, /pdf/sign, /pdf/validate, GET /publications, plus POST /cv/build for the narrative CV) instead of shelling out to Python itself. The service is reached only over a private network behind a shared secret compared in constant time, and refuses to start when that secret is unset or too short; nothing is persisted beyond a certificates volume and a disk-cached, rate-limited publications cache. Full diagram and detail: Architecture.md, "Layer 7 - Deployment (form-service HTTP API)".

docs.title: What lives where
docs.text:
Concern Owner PDF ingest contract, widget dump, filling, PAdES signing, HTTP transport ResearchTools (form-service skill + deploy/form-service/) Form catalogue, field maps, student profile ThesisTracker CV rendering (POST /cv/build, stateless, no LaTeX compiled, nothing stored) ResearchTools (narrative-cv skill) Student HQP rows, both consents (web publication and CV inclusion) ThesisTracker Twenty-two-unit delivery plan, shared data model, cross-repo decisions NEW_ARCHITECTURE.md (both repos)

When a plan changes something both sides depend on, NEW_ARCHITECTURE.md is the file that records it — update it there, in both checkouts, rather than in this manual.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
Chapter 10 of the ResearchTools manual. Back to table of contents.

Agents are specialists Claude delegates to automatically based on context, or explicitly on request ("use the scopus-auditor agent to…"). Twenty ship in this repo; most back a slash command. Two of them (local-writer, local-coder) are local-delegation agents: a cheap cloud wrapper that drives a local Ollama model over a Bash bridge (see "Local delegation"). Two are loop orchestrators: authoring-loop (ScholarEval-gated writing loop) and the code loop in the loop-engineer skill (see "Loop engineering").

Format (repo convention): one flat markdown file per agent at .claude/agents/<name>.md, opening with YAML frontmatter (name:, description:). This is what Claude Code's subagent discovery scans; a sub-folder layout is invisible to it. Note the asymmetry with skills, which ARE folder-based (skills/<name>/SKILL.md). The canonical .claude/agents/ files are the single source of truth; per-tool mirrors are generated from them (see "Using the agents outside Claude Code" below).

docs.title: latex-writer key rules
docs.text:
• TiKZ: relative positioning only (drawio2tikz-converted figures are the sanctioned absolute-coordinate exception); arrows perpendicular; no overlaps
  • References: peer-reviewed only (IEEE, Springer, Elsevier, Taylor & Francis, Cambridge, Wiley, IET, IOP, ACM, MDPI, ASME, ACME, BioMed Central (BMC)); DOI via hyperref; any other publisher needs user confirmation
  • Tables: rows = parameters, cols = concepts; bold headers; 10 % grey row shading
  • Language: French default for UQAC thesis, English for scientific papers
  • Avoid AI-detectable patterns: zero-width spaces, smart quotes, em dashes, perfect parallel lists

docs.title: reviewer-response key rules
docs.text:
• Reviewer files assigned sequentially: first file = R1, second = R2, etc.
  • Grammar-only fixes (G): applied directly, no markup
  • Additions \added[id=RN]{}, deletions \deleted[id=RN]{}, rewrites \replaced[id=RN]{}{} (changes package)
  • Reviewer colors: R1 blue, R2 red, R3 orange, R4+ purple (\definechangesauthor)
  • Every proposed reference validated via Scopus; [NO DOI] flagged in the summary when applicable

docs.title: Local delegation (Ollama subagents)
docs.text:
local-writer and local-coder cut cloud cost by keeping the top model as orchestrator and pushing token-heavy generation to local models on the GPU. Each agent runs on a cheap cloud model (Haiku) that only frames the task and drives a local model over ollama_bridge.py, which speaks Ollama's HTTP API and takes --role writer or --role coder instead of a model name; the bulk text or code is generated locally and free. Claude Code has one API endpoint per process and no per-subagent endpoint, so a subagent cannot be pointed at Ollama while the main session stays on Anthropic. That, and not the subscription, is why the Haiku wrapper drives the bridge, and only that small wrapper spends cloud tokens.

Requirements: Ollama running, and a qualified tag for the role you are about to use (model_resolver.py --resolve --role coder). There is no fallback tag: an unqualified role is an explicit stop, never a silent substitution of a weaker model. LiteLLM (~/.litellm/ollama.yaml) is optional and only gives the bridge its keep-alive / context tuning. local-writer never authors LaTeX prose (it may add % comments only); all scientific and LaTeX redaction stays with latex-writer + scientific-writing on the latest cloud Claude model.

aider-setup is a second, separate local-coding lane that needs no Claude Code at all — how it differs from local-coder and the nightly run itself: chapter 06.

docs.title: Loop engineering (local-model dev loop)
docs.text:
The loop-engineer skill runs a budget-bounded develop-and-improve loop: design → plan → code → comment → test → review → score → correct, repeating until a composite quality gate is met or a hard budget cap is hit. It keeps the best cloud model (Fable 5) as orchestrator/judge, uses cheaper cloud tiers (Opus for plans, Sonnet for execution and review) for the actions, and delegates code and comments to the local local-coder / local-writer agents so the heavy generation is free.

Option contract: --loop --budget <max_usd> --score <min_score> [--max-iters N]. The default stop gate is composite: tests green AND no CRITICAL/HIGH review findings AND aggregate score >= min_score (default 90); a literal 100 is opt-in. The loop also stops on the hard budget cap, the max-iterations cap, or a no-progress plateau. The score aggregates findings from the installed reviewers (/code-review, /security-guidance, pr-review-toolkit, systematic-debugging) plus the betterleaks / pip-audit hooks, with security as a hard floor (any CRITICAL fails the gate regardless of the aggregate). The final merge to a protected branch is human-gated: the loop stops at "ready to merge" and waits for your confirmation. The loop diagram and the use-case diagram are in Architecture.md ("Layer 5 — Loop engineering").

The same loop applies to writing through the authoring-loop agent (the ScholarEval-gated variant): define a subject, author with an authoring agent (/litreview, latex-writer, /replyreviewer, …) on Fable 5, audit with the scholar-evaluation skill on Sonnet or Haiku to get a score, loop until the ScholarEval target or the budget is reached, then record the learnings to memory via local-writer. The five steps are documented in the loop-engineer SKILL.md.

docs.title: Obsidian knowledge-capture loop
docs.text: Both loops read and write the Obsidian vault so learnings persist across iterations and projects (Claude Code has no cross-project memory of its own; the vault is that broad memory). local-writer is the single, serialized vault writer; local-coder reads only and hands it any learning. Reads happen at plan time (baked into the plan by brainstorming / writing-plans on the cloud tiers) and, during a run, only by the local agents (task start, checkpoints, error recovery); executing-plans does not read. Writes land in 10_Projets/<projet>/ logs and reusable 30_Ressources/ atomic notes through the outbox only - the SessionStart/SessionEnd obsidian-outbox-flush.py hook is the sole write path, never a fallback. The ~/bin/obsidian wrapper is for reads. Requires Obsidian open with the CLI enabled. Full design in docs/contributor-notes.md section 5; routing in .claude/CLAUDE.md.

docs.title: Calling an agent explicitly
docs.text:
Agents are normally triggered automatically by context. To invoke one directly, address it by name in your message:

Use the scopus-auditor agent to audit the review in paper_review/literature_review.tex

reviewer-response agent: --paper sn-article.tex --reviewers r1.txt --editor "Prof. Yin"

The slash commands /auditreview, /replyreviewer, /litreview, etc. are thin wrappers that call these agents with the same argument syntax — use the commands for convenience and the explicit agent names when you need finer control or want to chain agents in one message.

docs.title: Using the agents outside Claude Code
docs.text:
install.ps1 regenerates per-tool mirrors from the canonical .claude/agents/*.md files. Run it after adding or editing an agent, then commit the regenerated output. Add -Personal to also copy the Copilot agent profiles to ~/.copilot/agents/, which makes them available to Copilot CLI in every project (re-run after agent edits to refresh).

Tool Generated target Notes GitHub Copilot (agents) .github/agents/<name>.agent.md Auto-discovered once on the default branch (GitHub.com agents panel, coding agent, VS Code, Copilot CLI /agent or copilot --agent <name>). Copilot caps agent prompts at 30,000 characters, so the five large agents ship as stubs that read the canonical file first. GitHub Copilot (commands) .github/prompts/<name>.prompt.md One prompt file per task command (13); invoke as /<name> in Copilot Chat. The Claude session modes (concis, slim, focus, ctx) are skipped. GitHub Copilot (rules) .github/instructions/<name>.instructions.md One per .claude/rules/*.md, applied to all files (applyTo: "**"), plus the master .github/copilot-instructions.md (mission, agent routing, skills pointer). GitHub Copilot (skills) none needed Skills are plain repo folders (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md); Copilot agents read them directly, and the master instructions point there. Aider CONVENTIONS.md Pointer paragraph (created once, never overwritten). AGENTS.md readers (OpenHuman, Hermes Agent, Codex, and others) AGENTS.md Distilled master, regenerated on every run; agent list, routing pointer, skills examples, and the cross-cutting rules. Codex (skills) .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md Codex is the one harness with a native skill convention: it scans .agents/skills from the working directory up to the repo root. Each mirror is a pointer carrying only the frontmatter, since the description is the whole trigger surface and the body it then reads is the canonical file. Descriptions are trimmed to whole sentences to fit Codex's skill-list budget (8000 chars when the context window is unknown); over budget Codex shortens and then omits entries, so the trim is deliberate rather than left to chance. Codex (nested instructions) .claude/skills/AGENTS.md Codex concatenates one AGENTS.md per directory from the git root down to the working directory, later files overriding earlier ones, capped by project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB default). This one adds the script-surface rule for sessions working inside the skills tree.

For global availability in Claude Code (any working directory), install-junctions.ps1 links each .claude/agents/<name>.md into ~/.claude/agents/ per file (symlink; hard-link fallback when Developer Mode is off — re-run after a git pull that changes agents). Skills keep their per-folder junctions.

docs.title: Machine-local files (never committed)
docs.text:
The git privacy guard (.claude/hooks/git/, see 05-security-audit.md and security.md) is installed from repo-tracked source into three places, neither of the latter two part of the repository tree above:

  • Repo-side source, tracked: .claude/hooks/git/ — pre-commit, pre-push, privacy-lib.sh, privacy-extra.awk, privacy-guard.conf, fixture-path-allow.txt, privacy-rules.toml, install-git-hooks.ps1 (plus two files the installer reads here but never copies anywhere: deny-term-stopwords.txt, sync-folder-markers.txt).
  • Copied by the installer to ~/.config/git/hooks/ (core.hooksPath): pre-commit, pre-merge-commit (a copy of pre-commit, since a clean merge runs only that one), pre-push, _chain (plus one copy per other chained hook name), privacy-rules.toml, privacy-lib.sh, privacy-extra.awk, fixture-path-allow.txt, privacy-guard.conf.
  • Machine-local, never committed, and not inside any repository at all: live in the install folder, outside the tracked tree entirely, so they are not "gitignored files" so much as files no repository holds in the first place. What protects a stray copy pasted into a repository is the global git ignore the installer writes (core.excludesFile, else <XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config>/git/ignore), which also lists all three file names.
  • private-terms.txt — the generated deny list, extended for each new student (-TermsFrom <folder>): the installer only appends names it does not already have, never rewrites the list.
  • private-terms.extra.txt — hand-added terms.
  • private-terms.excluded.txt — fragments the extractor set aside (common words, or shorter than the configured length floor).

docs.title: Local coding and the cloud
docs.text:
Chapter 12 of the ResearchTools manual. Back to table of contents.

This chapter answers one question for any piece of coding: does it run on the cloud, through local-coder, through aider, or on a session you switched by hand, and who decides. It also says what the process costs, what stops it, and what the dashboard shows. The rule behind it is R38 in .claude/rules/workflows.md, and it binds every project on a machine where ResearchTools is installed.

docs.title: Why local coding exists
docs.text: A local model generates code on your GPU, so that generation costs no cloud tokens. The cloud still pays for the plan, for a small Haiku wrapper that drives the local model, and for the review of the result. Local coding saves tokens only while four things hold: the plan is dispatched to the local agent as a whole, the review loop is bounded, the explanation of the mechanism is correct, and you can see what the local model is doing. Four failures defeated it before this chapter: local-coder was never dispatched because it took one task per call, the review loop of R35 repeated until no finding with no maximum (seven unbounded iterations were measured on 2026-10-17), the documentation gave a wrong reason for the bridge, and local work was barely visible in the dashboard.

docs.title: The process
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Coding request<br/>superpowers:brainstorming"] --> B{Single step, no deliverable?}
    B -- yes --> C[Answer directly]
    B -- no --> D["Write spec, plans and progress<br/>superpowers:writing-plans"]
    D --> E[Ask the owner the bounds]
    E --> F[Write the header: executor, tier, bounds]
    F --> G{Which executor?}
    G -- judgment or no local role --> H["cloud: superpowers:executing-plans"]
    G -- one plan --> J[local-coder, Haiku wrapper and bridge]
    J --> K{Step output fits the coder window?}
    K -- yes --> L[tier simple or standard]
    K -- no --> M[tier large, session role]
    G -- several plans or night --> N[aider: writer and reviewer]
    H --> O[Worktree branch]
    L --> O
    M --> O
    N --> O
    O --> P[Review round on the diff]
    P --> Q{Findings?}
    Q -- none --> R[Pull request, owner merges]
    Q -- some --> S{Bound reached?}
    S -- no --> T[Fix, failing test first] --> P
    S -- yes --> U[Stop, ask the owner]
    F -.-> V[rt-observe follows every stage]

The source of this diagram is local-coding-flow.mmd, and a test fails when the two differ. Reading it from the top:

  • A request that is a single step with no deliverable of its own, such as reading one file, is answered directly. Anything larger gets plan files first.
  • The session asks you for the review bounds before it writes the plan header, because the header carries them.
  • The executor decision has three outcomes: the session itself runs the plan, one plan goes to local-coder, or several plans go to aider.
  • For local-coder the question is whether each step's prompt plus output fits the coder window. If it does not and the step cannot be split, the plan takes the large tier.
  • Every path ends in the same place: a worktree branch, a review round on its diff, and a pull request that you merge. A review round that still finds something is fixed with a failing test first, until a bound stops the loop and the session asks you.

docs.title: Choosing an executor
docs.text:
Situation Executor Why it saves cloud tokens Judgment, security, design, a repository-wide change, or no qualified local role The session itself, with executing-plans Nothing to save: the work needs the best model One plan, a test as oracle per step, each step's prompt plus output fits the coder window local-coder, tier simple or standard The cloud pays for the plan, the wrapper and the review; the code is generated locally One plan whose step output cannot fit the coder window and cannot be split local-coder, tier large Same, with a window large enough for long output Two or more plans, or an unattended night aider (spec, plan files, progress, a writer model and a reviewer model) No Claude Code is involved once the run starts A whole session on Ollama or Augure Your manual choice with claude-switch.ps1, never written in a plan The session itself is local

Fit is measured with context_budget.py --role and token_count.py, never guessed. A fix found by a review round is a small plan of its own and follows the same table.

docs.title: Plan files come first
docs.text:
Any coding request beyond a single step gets spec.md, plan<N>.md and progress.md before the first line of code, with the size ceilings below. Each plan opens with a header:

  • executor: local-coder, aider or cloud.
  • tier: simple, standard or large.
  • bounds: max_rounds, max_tokens and plateau, positive integers.

The cloud model writes executor and tier after asking you the bounds with a question that states what each choice costs. The bounds count input, cache creation and output tokens, with cache reads excluded, because money is not readable from this machine. plan_contract.py validate <plan> checks the header, the file limit of the tier and the size ceilings, and plan_contract.py resolve <plan> maps the tier to a resolver role. No plan names a model: the resolver names the tag at run time.

docs.title: A skill for every step
docs.text:
Rule R36 says that all tasks, any task, need a skill, or an agent that itself uses one. The process of this chapter obeys it at each step, so no step is run from memory. A step with no skill is a gap to report, never a step run without one.

Step Skill Notes Request superpowers:brainstorming Explores what is wanted before any plan exists Plan files superpowers:writing-plans Writes the spec, the plans and the progress ledger, with the header Execution superpowers:executing-plans Also loads test-driven development. A local-coder dispatch is made by a session that follows it Review code-review and security-review Under the bounds of R35 Pull request superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch You merge, never the session

A similar toolset may replace the three process skills, for example the speckit-* skills (speckit-specify, speckit-plan, speckit-tasks, speckit-implement), and the plan still names the skill used at each step. ruflow was named by the owner and is not installed or verified here, so no step relies on it. Aider is its own harness and sits outside this rule.

docs.title: Size ceilings
docs.text:
The ceilings are not written in the rules. They are the ceilings of .claude/skills/aider-setup/config/context-budget.json, the single source for every project, read when this chapter was written on 2026-10-17. The operator cut them on 2026-09-05 because every token of ceiling is reserved window, which is KV cache, which is model weights pushed off a small GPU.

File Ceiling in tokens spec.md 4000 plan.md 4000 progress.md 2048 audit.md 4096 code_file 16000

plan.md applies to each plan<N>.md. A test reads the budget file and fails when this table drifts from it. To count, run python .claude/skills/loop-engineer/scripts/token_count.py <file or folder>. With a tokenizer installed it uses the encoder aider uses and says the count is exact for that encoder. Without one it estimates characters over four and multiplies by 1.25 before a ceiling check, because real over estimated tokens ranged from 0.99 to 1.20 on the twelve files of this effort (measured 2026-10-17). It never calls an estimate exact. Three older counters remain on purpose, because the aider kit is standalone: Get-TokenCount in aider-plan-core.ps1, count_tokens in aider-rules-sync.py and estimate_tokens in context_budget.py.

docs.title: The four paths
docs.text:
The session runs the plan. The header says executor: cloud and the session follows executing-plans in a worktree. This is the path for judgment, security work, and any plan on a machine with no qualified local role.

One plan through local-coder. The dispatch prompt carries a line PLAN: <path>. The agent resolves the tier to a role with plan_contract.py resolve, generates each open step over the bridge, ticks progress.md with one of three marks and nothing else (- [ ] open, - [x] done, - [!] blocked), and reports. It audits nothing and never commits. Review runs in the calling session.

Several plans through aider. Aider keeps its own internal loop: a writer model codes and tests, and a different reviewer model audits and never edits. It reads spec.md, each plan<N>.md and progress.md, and a plan header does not change the files it names. See chapter 06.

A whole session switched by hand. claude-switch.ps1 provides claude-ollama, claude-augure and claude-cloud. This is your choice and is never written in a plan.

docs.title: Roles, windows and speed
docs.text:
A tier maps to a resolver role through plan-tiers.json, and the role to a model through the resolver. The figures below were read from the files that hold them when this chapter was written, and each row says where.

Tier Role Window Decode speed Source and date simple, standard coder 16384 tokens about 26.6 tokens per second Read 2026-10-17 from local-model-config.json (sweep by optimize_ollama.py) large session 262144 tokens, stored with --num-ctx about 2.4 tokens per second Adoption of 2026-10-09 in local-model-state.json, thread sweep by aider-thread-probe.py; the entry on this machine records no window yet any none qualified not applicable not applicable Read 2026-10-17: with no qualified role the plan runs on the cloud executor

The large tier is the Haiku wrapper plus the bridge with the session role. It is not a subagent on a local endpoint, which Claude Code does not offer. At about 2.4 tokens per second a 4000 token file takes roughly 28 minutes to generate, so use it only when a step truly cannot be split.

docs.title: What the Haiku wrapper does and costs
docs.text: local-coder and local-writer run on a cheap cloud model that frames the task, assembles one self-contained prompt, checks it fits the window, runs the bridge with the role, reads the result and writes it. The bridge speaks Ollama's HTTP API, asks the resolver for the model, and refuses rather than substituting a weaker one. The wrapper is the only cloud generation cost of a local step, and it is small because it never writes the code itself.

docs.title: Review bounds and the two hooks
docs.text:
Before the first review round the session asks you for the three bounds and runs loop_bounds.py init. After each round it runs loop_bounds.py tick --findings N. Two PreToolUse hooks enforce the contract, both declared in settings.template.json, and each exits silently when its dependency is absent:

  • review-loop-guard.py guards the review skills. It refuses with the command to run when no bounds are declared, and with the bound reached when max_rounds, max_tokens or the plateau is spent. A refused call does not consume a round.
  • local-coder-dispatch-guard.py guards the dispatch of local-coder. It refuses a prompt with no PLAN: line, a plan outside the repository or over a ceiling, a plan whose executor is not local-coder, and a plan whose tier has no qualified role.

Messages you will meet: "no review-loop bounds are declared for this branch" with the init command, "max_rounds reached for code-review", and "a local-coder dispatch must name its plan". When a bound stops the loop before a clean round, the session reports what remains and asks you whether to raise it. It never opens the pull request on its own.

docs.title: Every project, and the cloud fallback
docs.text: Once ResearchTools is installed the contract binds every project on the machine: the rule is in the exported part of .claude/CLAUDE.md, the rules folder is shared, and the hooks come from the settings template. On a machine with no qualified model for the tier, plan_contract.py resolve returns the cloud executor with the reason, and the plan is executed in the session. It never falls back to a weaker local model.

docs.title: What the dashboard shows
docs.text: rt-observe follows the work from three snapshot sections. local_calls reads a bounded tail of the bridge log and shows each role with its model, window, calls, tokens and whether it is active. rounds lists each plan of a round folder with its executor, tier and task counts, and the review loop of every worktree as rounds used of the maximum. The Real-Time tab draws a lane and a token ring for each active bridge role, and shows an aider run's fixed cost and task budget. See chapter 07.

docs.title: What is verified, unsupported and untried
docs.text:
Read from the Claude Code documentation on 2026-10-17:

  • Claude Code has one API endpoint per process and no per-subagent endpoint, environment or provider, so a subagent cannot be pointed at Ollama while the main session stays on Anthropic. That, and not the subscription, is why local models go through the bridge.
  • Switching the whole session with claude-switch.ps1 works and was measured here, but Anthropic documents that it does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through a gateway, and Remote Control is unavailable while the base URL is not api.anthropic.com.
  • A model ID Claude Code does not recognise is assumed to have a 200K window unless CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS is set. Whether that variable is capped at the model's own window is not documented and is untried here.

Also untried until one live firing on this machine: that both hooks fire on their matchers.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• A review is refused with no bounds: ask for the three bounds, then run the init command the message names. Whether a review typed by hand reaches the hook is unverified, so declare --max-rounds 1 first as the one-shot.
  • A dispatch is refused: add the PLAN: line, or fix the header key the message names.
  • The plan resolves to the cloud: no model is qualified for the tier's role. Qualify one with the resolver, or run the plan in the session.
  • The session role has no window: adopt it again with --num-ctx, then try claude-local once.
  • The page shows no local lane: the bridge log has no record with a role yet, and the section says why instead of drawing an empty panel.
